rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters associate partners with God because they fail to grasp His true majesty and measure Him by limited human standards.
rows.anchor: they have not appreciated the true majesty and exaltedness of God. They have measured God with their limited scales.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their limited scale confuses a ray with the sun and a drop with the ocean, exposing the absurdity of comparing deities with God.
rows.anchor: they have not been able to distinguish between a ray of light and the sun, between a drop of water and the ocean.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Judgment, the earth is as a handful in God's grasp and the heavens are folded in His hands, displaying His unmatched power.
rows.anchor: this whole earth will be in God’s grasp like a handful of sand

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word qabḍah means an amount of something picked up as a handful.
rows.anchor: قبضة refers to that quantity of a thing which is picked up as a handful.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that God is exalted above their associations means such associations oppose both His holiness and His exaltedness.
rows.anchor: Such associations are not only against His holiness but also His exaltedness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters imagined their deities were close to God, could secure benefits for worshippers, and could protect them from God through their influence.
rows.anchor: these deities are very close to God and would win such and such things for their worshippers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the first trumpet blast, every creature on earth falls unconscious except those God chooses to spare.
rows.anchor: when the trumpet is sounded for the first time, every creature on earth will fall down unconscious

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the second trumpet blast, everyone rises and looks around in amazement.
rows.anchor: when the trumpet is sounded for a second time, everyone will rise up and look here and there in amazement.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trumpet's overwhelming power refutes any claim that deities can intercede by cajoling God or stand as His peers.
rows.anchor: who can dare try to advocate and intercede for someone before God by cajoling Him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception indicates that some will be spared unconsciousness, but the author says their identity is difficult to determine.
rows.anchor: It is difficult to give a definite answer to this question.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tentatively suggests that the angels glorifying God around the Throne are spared the trumpet's effect, while stressing this is only a hint and he is not confident.
rows.anchor: angels who would be glorifying and extolling God around His throne will be the ones who will not be effected by the trumpet sound. This is merely a hint.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth that appears at Judgment is a transformed earth operating under new laws, as described in 14:48.
rows.anchor: The earth referred to here is the one which will come into existence on the Day of Judgement with new laws.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike today's earth lit by the sun, the new earth shines by God's light, revealing many more facts; its nature exceeds the expressive capacity of human language.
rows.anchor: that earth will be lit up by the light of God; hence, many more facts and details will come before people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unveiling described in 50:22 makes realities beyond present eyesight observable on the new earth.
rows.anchor: today what eyes do not have the power to observe will become observable in the earth which will later come to being.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth will disclose its history at God's prompting, and divine radiance will make now-hidden facts visible even to those presently blind and deaf.
rows.anchor: on that Day, these facts will light up from the radiance of God is such a manner that these people who today have become blind and deaf will also see them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book, prophetic and other testimony, and fair judgment are effects of God's radiance: the threatened reward and punishment will become manifest as veils lift.
rows.anchor: refer to the affects of the appearance of God’s light and radiance: the reward and punishment with which people are being warned of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Context indicates that the book placed before people is the register of their accounts.
rows.anchor: Contextual indication shows that it refers to the register of accounts of people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets will testify about what they taught their peoples and how those peoples responded; the Qur'an discusses this in detail in Sūrah Mā’idah.
rows.anchor: The Almighty will ask the prophets to bear witness to what they taught their people and what was their response.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general term witnesses includes any humans or angels able to testify in a matter.
rows.anchor: those people shall also be called forth who will be in a position to bear witness in some matter whether they are from among human beings or from among the angels.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this community is God's witnesses on earth, its reformers and righteous people will be summoned and questioned about their teaching and people's response.
rows.anchor: this ummah is داءهش اللّٰہ في رضلأَا God’s witnesses on earth) hence the reformers and the righteous will also be summoned

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After testimony, each person's account is judged fairly, without the slightest injustice.
rows.anchor: the account of each person will be judged with fairness and not the slightest of injustice will be done to anyone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that none is wronged means every soul receives exactly what its deeds merit, like harvesting what one planted.
rows.anchor: each person shall reap what he sowed and what he will receive will be fully commensurate with his deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot forget any deed: He fully knows what people do and has everything clearly written in His register.
rows.anchor: there is no possibility that God will forget any deed of a person; He is fully aware of what people are doing and everything is clearly written down in His register.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These details aim to awaken the idolaters to the baselessness of their hopes and the reality awaiting them.
rows.anchor: The purpose of all these details is to open the eyes of the Idolaters so that they realize how baseless are their desires

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers under discussion are the idolaters; associating partners with God is disbelief, since only pure monotheism is acceptable and shirk contaminates belief.
rows.anchor: polytheism ( shirk) is disbelief ( kufr). Only that belief in God is considerable to Him which is based on pure monotheism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the witnesses testify, all guilty of disbelief are led to Hell, whose seven gates receive groups classified by their sins.
rows.anchor: once these testimonies end all those guilty of disbelief will be led to Hell. Once they come near it, its gates will be opened.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell's keepers rebuke the doomed by asking whether messengers came to recite God's revelations and warn them of this meeting.
rows.anchor: they will rebuke them on seeing their horrible fate and ask them whether messengers of God came to them to inform them of the horrors of this Day.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doomed acknowledge messengers came, but their own wretched response caused God's punishment to be imposed on them.
rows.anchor: these people will confess their crime and say that messengers did come to them yet it was their wretched response

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'decree of punishment' refers to God's comprehensive decision, announced to Satan, that whoever follows Satan will enter Hell with him.
rows.anchor: refers to the total decision of God which He pronounced before Satan in response to the latter’s challenge.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah Mulk gives a fuller confession: the condemned rejected the warner, denied revelation, and regret that they neither listened nor reasoned.
rows.anchor: Thus the words of Sūrah Mulk are: اَمَّلُك َيِقْلُأُ اَهیِف جٌْوَف ْمُهَلَأََس اَهُتَنَزَخ ْمَلَأُ ْمُكِتْأََی رٌیِذَن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After confessing, the disbelievers are ordered to enter Hell permanently.
rows.anchor: they will be told to enter the gates of Hell and this entry is forever.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them arrogant identifies the cause of their evasion and rejection: pride made them reject truth and merits Hell, an abode reserved for the arrogant.
rows.anchor: it is out of sheer arrogance that they evaded the truth and became worthy of this abode which has been specially reserved for the arrogant.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb suq means to lead or drive, in either a positive or negative sense; it describes both mercy-bearing clouds and the Hell-bound, while here it positively describes the righteous being led to Paradise.
rows.anchor: The word سوق means to lead or drive something to something. It is used both in the positive and the negative sense.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels surround the righteous on every side and escort them to Paradise in their company and custody.
rows.anchor: in front of them and behind the righteous as well as on their left and right there will be angels of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional sentence's answer is suppressed, as in 37:103–105; its eloquence and occasion are discussed in that passage's commentary.
rows.anchor: The answer to the conditional clause in this verse is suppressed. A similar example of such suppression can be seen in verses 103-105 of Sūrah S @āffāt.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response is suppressed because its meaning can exceed what words express; silence can convey what speech cannot.
rows.anchor: At times, such is the nature of the answer of a conditional clause or sentence that words are unable to express it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The welcome word means a wish that the entrants remain happy, comfortable, and prosperous.
rows.anchor: مُتْبِط is a word of welcome. It is like saying: “May you always be happy! May you always live in happiness and comfort!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing contrast with disbelievers: fear kept them from arrogance, so they listened to and accepted God's messengers.
rows.anchor: since these people feared God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised bliss is beyond present imagination; another Qur'anic passage says no soul knows what joy is hidden for it.
rows.anchor: At that time, what they will acquire cannot be imagined by anyone today.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land they inherit is Paradise, the land introduced in 39:69.
rows.anchor: The word land ( ضْرَأُhere refers to the land of Paradise which is mentioned earlier in verse 69.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing God's promises through His prophets and messengers fulfilled one by one, Paradise's inhabitants spontaneously thank Him for fulfilling them and granting them its land to inhabit at will.
rows.anchor: When the dwellers of Paradise will see that the promises made by God through his prophets and messengers have been fulfilled one by one, then their tongues will spontaneously thank God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inheritance subtly recalls that Paradise was given to Adam, lost through Satan's temptation, and regained by his descendants who enter the world and defeat Satan in a test.
rows.anchor: this Paradise was given to Adam (sws) their father; however, Satan deprived him of it by luring him away

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their gratitude expresses success in the trial and recovery of the Paradise their father lost.
rows.anchor: these people of Paradise will express their gratitude that they have been successful in this test and they have regained the Paradise lost by their father.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freedom to dwell wherever they wish means no obstacle will prevent their desires or intentions from being realized in Paradise.
rows.anchor: will full liberty and authority they will move around in Paradise wherever they want to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's reality is unimaginable now and will be known only in a new world, with new laws and human capacities, lit by the Lord rather than the sun.
rows.anchor: this new world will appear with its new laws and mankind also appears in it with new strengths and abilities, and this new earth will shine with the radiance of its Lord instead of that of the sun.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excellent reward of the righteous is set in exact contrast to the evil abode of the arrogant in 39:72.
rows.anchor: The part َمْعِنَف ُرْجَأُ َنیِلِامَعْال occurs in exact contrast to َسْئُِبَف ىَوْثَم َنیِرِّبَكَتُمْال of verse
